title: The Midnight Crown Again
premise: Ulyana Pemberton has spent two decades hiding her magic in Cinderhollow, a city where the Magistrate's Wardens burn hedge-witches, until a chance meeting with a stranger named Corin reveals his face in 'The Ashen Hours,' a century-old book of prophecies she was meant to destroy. The prophecy names them both: the witch who fled and the man whose soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain before he was born. To free Corin and stop the last dragon-fire from guttering out—which would unleash the starving things sealed beneath the city—Ulyana must return to the coven that raised her, bargain with the mountain court's exiled queen, and finally pay the debt her own survival cost. In the end, Ulyana chooses love over invisibility, trading her hidden years for Corin's soul, and together they rekindle the dragon-fire at the price of the old world's silence.
about_author: Wendell Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent eleven years cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people who survive by staying small, and live in a drafty house full of books that occasionally hum.

chapters.title: Charms for the Fearful
chapters.summary: Ulyana sells luck-knots and fever-charms in Cinderhollow's night market, hiding her craft behind merchant's patter while Wardens patrol. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: the exhausting vigilance of a life built on being overlooked.

chapters.title: The Stranger Who Ordered Tea
chapters.summary: A quiet man named Corin asks Ulyana for a charm against forgetting; something in his presence feels hollowed out. She refuses him, then can't stop thinking about him. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: reluctant recognition of loneliness mirrored.

chapters.title: The Book That Should Have Burned
chapters.summary: Sorting her late mentor's effects, Ulyana finds 'The Ashen Hours,' a prophecy book she was ordered to destroy as an apprentice—and sees Corin's face inked on its pages beside her own. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: dread blooming into terrible curiosity.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Small Magic
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Ulyana flees the Thornhollow coven after refusing the rite that binds apprentices to the mountain court, leaving her sister-apprentice Brenna behind. POV: Ulyana (past). Emotional beat: the wound that made hiding feel like freedom.

chapters.title: Wardens at the Door
chapters.summary: A Warden raid sweeps her street; Ulyana hides her charms and watches a neighbor's daughter dragged away for a candle-spell. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: guilt—the safety she buys costs others everything.

chapters.title: Corin's Empty Year
chapters.summary: Corin tells Ulyana he has no memories before age nineteen and wakes each night tasting ash; she realizes his soul was sold at birth, exactly as the prophecy describes. POV: alternating Ulyana/Corin. Emotional beat: two broken people recognizing the same fracture.

chapters.title: The Prophecy Read Backward
chapters.summary: Deciphering 'The Ashen Hours,' Ulyana learns the last dragon-fire beneath the mountain keeps worse things sealed—and it gutters out within a season unless a sold soul returns home. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: the weight of inevitability.

chapters.title: Brenna's Letter
chapters.summary: A crow delivers a letter from Brenna, now the coven's High Witch: come home, or we come for you. The coven knows the fire is dying too. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: the past demanding its due.

chapters.title: What Hiding Cost
chapters.summary: Ulyana burns her charm stock and closes her stall, saying goodbye to the market family that never knew her. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: grief for the small safe life she's choosing to lose.

chapters.title: Road Through the Ash Country
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Corin travel toward Thornhollow through land scarred by the old dragon wars, pursued by a Warden tracker named Sergeant Ilse Vane. POV: Ulyana. Emotional bond deepening between the pair; first real danger.

chapters.title: The Inn Without Mirrors
chapters.summary: At an inn where mirrors are banned, Corin catches no reflection at all—proof his soul is elsewhere. A dying hedge-witch gives Ulyana a map to the mountain court's back door. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: tenderness sharpened by horror.

chapters.title: Vane Catches Up
chapters.summary: Ilse Vane corners them at a river crossing; Ulyana uses real magic for the first time in twenty years to escape, revealing herself. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: exhilaration and terror of being seen.

chapters.title: Thornhollow Gates
chapters.summary: Ulyana returns to the coven that raised her; Brenna greets her with cold ceremony and warmer eyes than her words allow. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: homecoming as confrontation.

chapters.title: The Rite She Refused
chapters.summary: Brenna explains why the binding rite matters: the mountain court feeds on bound souls, and unbound witches like Ulyana are the only ones who can enter and leave freely. POV: Ulyana/Brenna. Emotional beat: understanding reframing old betrayal.

chapters.title: Coven Politics
chapters.summary: The coven elders want to use Corin as bait to bargain with the court; Ulyana refuses, splitting the sisters. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against survival logic.

chapters.title: Lessons in Old Fire
chapters.summary: An ancient coven teacher, Mother Ysolde, trains Ulyana in fire-magic she abandoned, forcing her to relive the night she ran. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Corin Remembers Something
chapters.summary: Near the mountain, Corin begins dreaming fragments of the court below—a throne of teeth, a queen with his mother's voice. POV: Corin. Emotional beat: identity trembling at the edge of recovery.

chapters.title: The Queen in Exile
chapters.summary: They find Seraiva, the mountain court's deposed queen, hiding in a drowned chapel; she claims only she can open the way down, and her price is steep. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: wary alliance with someone beautiful and dangerous.

chapters.title: Seraiva's Price
chapters.summary: The exiled queen wants Ulyana's twenty hidden years—the memories themselves—as payment for passage. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh: what is survival worth?

chapters.title: Vane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ilse Vane, disgraced after the river escape, offers Ulyana a deal: deliver the prophecy book to the Magistrate and Corin goes free. POV: Vane. Emotional beat: the antagonist revealed as another woman surviving by duty.

chapters.title: The Night Market Burns
chapters.summary: Retaliatory Warden fires destroy Ulyana's old market; friends she abandoned are hurt. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: hiding protected no one—her invisibility was always a lie.

chapters.title: Descent Preparations
chapters.summary: The coven arms Ulyana with salt-iron and song-charms; Brenna finally admits she reported Ulyana's location years ago to save her from a worse fate. POV: Ulyana/Brenna. Emotional beat: forgiveness, imperfect but real.

chapters.title: Into the Mountain
chapters.summary: Guided by Seraiva, the party enters the court beneath the mountain through a throat of cooling lava tunnels. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: claustrophobic courage.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: They witness the soul-market: bottled lives traded by pale courtiers while the great dragon Ember-that-Waits lies dimming on a hoard of spent years. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: awe curdled into pity.

chapters.title: The Queen of Teeth
chapters.summary: The usurper queen Mavrosa recognizes Seraiva and captures the party; she offers Corin his soul back if Ulyana surrenders the prophecy book. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Cellar of Bottled Souls
chapters.summary: Imprisoned, Ulyana finds Corin's soul in a jar labeled with his true name—Aldous Vane, the tracker's stolen brother. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: the personal stakes detonate.

chapters.title: What Ilse Lost
chapters.summary: Flashback: Ilse Vane sold her infant brother's soul to buy the family's survival from the Magistrate, and has hunted supernatural answers ever since. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: villain becomes mirror.

chapters.title: Escape by Song
chapters.summary: Mother Ysolde's song-charm lets Ulyana slip her cell; she frees Seraiva but must leave Corin behind as leverage. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: the agony of strategic abandonment.

chapters.title: Ember-that-Waits
chapters.summary: Ulyana reaches the dying dragon, who shows her the truth: the court's queens have been feeding it souls for centuries to keep the seals shut—and it is starving anyway. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: compassion for the monster holding up the world.

chapters.title: The Deal Refused
chapters.summary: Mavrosa offers Ulyana everything—Corin whole, her old life restored—if she hands over the book and walks away invisible again. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: the final temptation of her lifelong instinct.

chapters.title: Choosing to Be Seen
chapters.summary: Ulyana refuses, declaring herself aloud with her true name and craft, shattering Mavrosa's claim over hidden things. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: liberation through self-declaration.

chapters.title: Ilse Turns
chapters.summary: Ilse Vane arrives with Warden forces intending to burn the court, but Ulyana shows her brother's soul-jar; Ilse switches sides mid-siege. POV: Ilse/Ulyana. Emotional beat: enemy becoming ally through shared grief.

chapters.title: The Throne of Teeth Falls
chapters.summary: Together they overthrow Mavrosa; Seraiva takes the throne but refuses to keep feeding souls to the fire, forcing the real problem into the open. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: victory that solves nothing by itself.

chapters.title: The Price Named
chapters.summary: Ember-that-Waits will die unless fed willingly; the only sufficient offering is a soul freely given—and Ulyana's unbound, twenty-years-hidden soul is the strongest left. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: the bill comes due.

chapters.title: Corin's Choice
chapters.summary: Restored to his body and memories, Aldous refuses to let Ulyana pay; he argues the fire took enough of him already—he owes it nothing. POV: Aldous/Corin. Emotional beat: love arguing against sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Giving
chapters.summary: Ulyana gives not her whole soul but her twenty hidden years—all the time she spent invisible—pouring them into the dragon, which blazes back to life. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: sacrifice that costs identity without ending love.

chapters.title: Seals Renewed
chapters.summary: With the fire roaring, the seals hold; Seraiva reforms the court around consent rather than theft, and freed souls—including the market prisoners—return above. POV: multiple. Emotional beat: a better world built from an old machine.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Cinderhollow
chapters.summary: Weeks later, magic is decriminalized under the new accord; Ulyana reopens her stall openly, teaching frightened neighbors small safe charms. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not granted.

chapters.title: What She Cannot Remember
chapters.summary: Ulyana grieves the lost twenty years—faces and kindnesses gone—even as Aldous patiently retells her own life to her. POV: Ulyana/Aldous. Emotional beat: mourning and intimacy intertwined.

chapters.title: The Midnight Crown Again
chapters.summary: On the year's longest night, Ulyana and Aldous crown the waking dragon with ember-light per the prophecy's final verse; the book 'The Ashen Hours' writes one new line—hers, chosen, unwritten until now. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: quiet triumph; the story ends with a future instead of a fate.
